PM +24%; escapes -91.8% [89.9,93.5] (driven by costless full inspection; blind+full alone -91.4%); +$5471/ep, wins 96%. SPEC §4.2 scorecard was unmeasured targets -> replaced. Docs corrected (README, COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN, SPEC, benchmark_report). Replay 0/480 mismatches; run_ab and verify_ab agree exactly. title: Engine design: 'full' inspection is free -> escape metric dominated by one costless knob
description: quality.CATCH_PROB full=0.97 vs sample=0.65 with identical inspect proc time and no per-mode cost. blind+full alone cuts escapes 93% (verify run, 2000 seeds). Any agent should always pick full; inspect_mode is not a decision. Consider per-mode inspect time or cost. Also: per-tick station state + ops_seen leaks every op's cycle time (free SPC), making the probe budget near-redundant. From amdrome-bqm.

title: Engine: understaffing speeds stations up (staffing multiplier divides proc time)
description: core.py step 9: s.remaining = proc_time / roster.staffing_multiplier(kind). labour.UNDERSTAFF_PROC_PENALTY=1.3 (0 workers) => 23% FASTER; DOUBLE_STAFF_BONUS=0.9 (2 workers) => 11% SLOWER. Name/docstring say proc-time multiplier, so it should multiply. Found during A/B verification (amdrome-bqm). Fix requires golden-hash re-pin + gate re-run.

comments.author: dawn
comments.text: FIXED: 8ed7aff (staffing now multiplies proc time) + d9a7ed8 (skill->defect sign was ALSO inverted: low skill gave fewer defects). Regression tests fail before the fixes and pass after; golden v8->v9. Before/after (n=1000 paired, seeds 960000+): reactive-blind +2181 (dz .77) -> +2858 (dz .87); assistant-blind dz 1.60 -> 1.69; ordering preserved; anti-tape PASS (9.5/3/9.5 -> 9/2/8%). Labour decision's own edge ~nil either way (+24 -> +175) because assign is counts-only -> amdrome-qwv. New exploit after the fix: throttling (all workers on pack) beats blind +1850 -> amdrome-48q. Note research/2026-10-17-labour-svf.md.

title: Labour API: assign takes counts only, so affinity matching is impossible
description: Roster.apply_assignment/roll_shift fill each station with pool[:n] from present workers in ROSTER ORDER. An agent can't choose WHICH worker goes where, so 'specialist-to-station matching' (the stated labour skill) can't be expressed; reactive._assignment's affinity logic only sets counts. Measured (amdrome-svf, 1000 paired seeds): reactive vs reactive-without-assign edge is +$24 pre-fix (z 0.3) and +$175 post-fix (z 2.1), roughly nil. Proposal: accept {station: [worker_id,...]} and keep counts as a fallback.

title: Economics: throttling the line beats blind (unstaff exploit +$1.85k/ep after the svf fix)
description: After amdrome-svf, piling every worker onto pack (5 stations unstaffed, 1.3x slower) beats blind by +$1850/ep (d_z 0.59, wins 72%): fewer ops means less wear, fewer breakdowns (3.11 vs 4.21) and less downtime, which outweighs ~3 fewer clean units. Under run-to-failure the marginal unit loses money. Reactive still beats the exploit by ~$1k. Decide whether this is the intended 'discipline gradient' or whether unit margin should rise. Data: research/data/svf/.
